page.layout: One page of running text in a single column. One note in the right margin, beside "Sextus est". Catchword and signature at the foot. The left edge of the neighbouring page is not transcribed.

main_text.p: tura promittuntur bona, per horas singulas & momenta considerans, & immensum Dei beneficiorum pelagus attendens, dicebat, QVID RETRIBVAM DOMINO PRO OMNIBVS, &c. Sic ille. Observate, obsecro, Patris hujus sanctissimi, juxtà & doctissimi, Dialecticam. Si millies moriendo pro Christo, nullâ tamen virtute nostrâ beneficiis praeteritis nos digni judicandi simus; multò minùs digni censendi sumus futuris illis, quæ præterita excellunt non minùs, quàm immensorum bonorum pelagus vilium pugillum donorum, non obstante quantacunque virtutis nostræ æstimatione. Sic enim ait, Etsi omnes virtutes animi expleamus.

Sextus est{k} Autor operis imperfecti, scriptor sanè perantiquus: NON SUNT CONDIGNÆ, &c. Si ergò major erit gloria, quàm quod Sanctorum unusquisque meretur; quomodo aliis sufficiat ad salutem opus illorum, cùm nec sibi solis sufficiat ad gloriam justo judi-tio[?] consequendam? — Quid ergò dignum faciemus in hoc sæculo, ut participes Domini nostri in regnis cælestibus facti simus? Ideo dixit Apostolus, NON SUNT CONDIGNÆ PASSIONES, &c. Sic ille. Cujus consequentia est nostra conclusio, Non esse condignas passiones, &c. At est ejus ratio una ex nostris præmissis: non solùm quia remuneratio passionem excellat, sed quia nemo sufficiat sibi ad gloriam consequendam.In Matt. hom.52,53.

page.notes: Running head "Sect. 3." reads faintly; the "3" may be a different figure. The word "Sicille." on the first line could be "Sic ille." with a tight space. "judi-tio" at the line break is read with [?]. The first word "tura" is a fragment of a word from the previous page and stays as printed. The large italic capitals in the text are printed as shown. The left strip showing "14." and fragments of the neighbouring page is not transcribed. Italic boundaries are approximate where the scan is soft.
